body.statement: Let \((Q_1,Q_2,A_1,A_2)\) be the centered Gaussian limit of the pre-period loss and ATT coordinates, and let \((R_1,R_2)\) be the centered Gaussian post-period limit, independent of the pre-period limit. For each \(s\in\mathcal S\), the fitted-score Bartlett estimator with \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\) satisfies \(\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}\to_{P_n}V_s\) and \(\Pr_{P_n}\{\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}>0\}\to1\). Consequently, \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau)\Rightarrow A_{J(d)}+\sqrt rR_{J(d)}\), and \((\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau)/\widehat{\operatorname{se}}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\widehat J}\Rightarrow T_1\mathbf 1\{X\leq k\}+T_2\mathbf 1\{X>k\}\). This strictly extends the fixed-role limit of Shi et al. (2026) to the nonregular local role-selection boundary while reducing to that result when \(|d|\to\infty\).
body.justification: The theorem identifies the actual first-order law reported after outcome-based donor/proxy role choice.
body.gap: Shi et al. derive normality only for a predetermined role, while Lee et al. target a conditional selective pivot rather than this switched causal coordinate.
body.consumer: An analyst comparing two scientifically credible West-German role assignments can calculate the asymptotic law of the reported conventional proximal ATT.
